thread:
sam: Pushed a new Next starter template (edge runtime + LlamaIndex KV sample). Quick heads-up: seeing 401s during SSR fetches and the browser SDK streaming isn't available. Wanted to flag here before we promote it to the docs site.

marta: ugh, 401 during SSR — is that the access token missing in server-side fetch? which auth flow are you using?

sam: using the client-side short-lived token pattern we recommended in the quickstart: we set RW_API_KEY in server env for local dev, but SSR pages call the internal /api/proxy which forwards to Redwood API. The server logs show: "token_expired" on the call.

june: can you paste the proxy handler? often it's a fetch() call that doesn't forward cookies/headers properly when using Next edge. also edge envs disallow some Node libs.

sam: snippet: ```js
export default async function handler(req) {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.RW_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(req.body)
  })
  return new Response(await res.text(), { status: res.status })
}
```

liam: that looks fine but on edge you need to use globalThis.fetch and can't rely on some env behavior. Also if you're rotating keys in dev, make sure process.env is available to the edge function — Next edge runtime can't access process.env at runtime the same way. Try storing a token in a secret-managed server route and fetch from there.

marta: also saw the browser SDK streaming missing — what's the package.json version of @redwood/inference-js? streaming is only in >=3.1.0 for browser.

sam: ahhh we were on 3.0.2. Will upgrade. For SSR token expiry, switching to server-only token endpoint fixed it locally (server route reads secret and proxies). But we still hit duplicate completions when the proxy retries on 502. Need retry semantics to be idempotent for streaming/long-completions.

june: important: our default SDK retry will re-POST same request. For generation calls that are not idempotent, add an idempotency key header (eg: x-rw-idempotency) and the server will dedupe within 30s. We should add that to the starter template.

liam: note re: streaming parity: browser client had streaming via response.body.getReader(); Node client used eventsource stream helper. Parity issue: browser didn't expose a simple onMessage API like Node. We'll sync APIs in the next SDK patch so Starter doesn't need hacks.

sam: filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/starter/issues/48 — summary in case folks want to follow. Plan: (1) bump SDK to 3.1.x, (2) change proxy to server-only (no edge runtime), (3) add idempotency header and a note about retries, (4) add a small eval harness integration that verifies streaming + KV cache correctness in CI.

marta: for the eval harness - can we wire Redwood Optimize checks? I'd like a simple smoke eval that asserts latency < 300ms and that embeddings/kv hits are working. Could be a Jest test that mocks traffic and asserts cache hit metric via the /metrics endpoint.

june: agree, but don't rely on prod metrics in the starter CI. Add a lightweight local KV mock and test that prefix cache is used. Also add an integration test that runs against the hosted sandbox and is opt-in via env (like CI_CANARY=true).

liam: I'll follow up and open a PR to the SDK to expose browser streaming callback hook and add proper doc examples for edge vs server runtimes.

sam: thanks everyone. I'll update the starter repo with the idempotency header and the proxy change. Leaving the GH issue with checklist. If anyone wants to pair on the eval harness PR ping me. :rocket:
